India
Royal Holloway has very strong links with India, with appromxiately 500 Indian students currently enrolled at the university. We also maintain strong connections with top Indian universities, including OP Jindal, Chandigarh and Shoolini. Royal Holloway has been welcoming Indian students for many years and we are proud to have a vibrant community on campus.
Royal Holloway’s strong connection with India extends far beyond graduation. Recent alumni events in Delhi, Bengaluru and Mumbai brought together graduates from across industries to network, reconnect and share their professional journeys with university leaders and current staff. With more than 1,350 Royal Holloway alumni based in India, students joining our community become part of a truly global network that supports career growth, international opportunities and lifelong connections.
We are a pioneering university, steeped in history and culture, yet constantly evolving and adapting to the demands of modern higher education.
Our University was founded by two social reformers who pioneered the ideal of education and knowledge for all who could benefit. Their vision lives on today. As one of the UK’s leading research-intensive universities, we are home to some of the world’s foremost authorities in the sciences, arts, business, economics and law. As teachers and researchers they change lives, expand minds and help current and future leaders understand power and responsibility. We are strengthened by diversity, and welcome students and academics who travel from all over the world to study and work here, ensuring an international and multi-cultural perspective within a close-knit and historic campus.

Undergraduate Entry Requirements
Higher Secondary School Certificate
Students who have completed their Higher Secondary Certificate in India will be considered for direct entry onto our undergraduate programmes. The entry requirement will depend on on the subject you are planning to study at Royal Holloway, but most departments will require an overall grade of 80% to 85% with 85% in any subjects specified in GCE A-level entry requirements for the course.
Students who have completed their Diploma of Secondary will need to take our one year International Foundation Year or International Year One programme, or the equivalent from another institution, before beginning their undergraduate studies.
A levels & International Baccalaureate (IB)
If you have taken A levels or the IB, you will be considered for direct entry onto our undergraduate programmes. Specific grade requirements can be found in the course finder entry for your chosen course.
University preparation programmes
The Royal Holloway International Study Centre provides an International Foundation Year and International Year One programme, which are designed for international students who do not quite meet the requirements for an undergraduate course. These programmes will help to develop your academic and English language skills in preparation for university. Upon successful completion, you can progress to degree level study at Royal Holloway, University of London.
Postgraduate Entry Requirements
Masters Degree
Students who have successfully completed a Bachelors degree in an appropriate subject with good grades/GPA will be considered for entry to a Royal Holloway Master's degree programme. Exact requirements will depend upon the programme you are planning to study at Royal Holloway and the university you have studied at, but departments will usually require an overall grade between a 55% to 65%.
Research Degree (MPhil/PhD)
Students who have successfully completed a Masters degree in an appropriate subject with good grades/GPA will be considered for entry to a Royal Holloway MPhil/PhD programme. Exact requirements will depend upon the programme you are planning to study at Royal Holloway.
The Royal Holloway International Study Centre
The Royal Holloway International Study Centre provides Pre-Masters Programme, which are designed for international students who do not quite meet the requirements for a postgraduate course. These programmes will help to develop your academic and English language skills in preparation for university. Upon successful completion, you can progress to degree level study at Royal Holloway, University of London.
Acceptance of MOI from select Indian Universities
At Royal Holloway, we are able to accept a Bachelor's or Master’s degree completed at the following Indian universities as proof of English competency.
MOI (Medium of Instruction) acceptance is valid for 3 years from the end of your degree. We require your final certificate and transcripts to assess MOI, or an explicit MOI declaration demonstrating that your degree was taught in English.
Anna University
Ashoka University
IISc Bangalore
Indian Institutes of Technology - IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Kanpur, IIT Kharagpur, IIT Madras
Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad
Op Jindal Global University
Shoolini University
SRM Institute of Science and Technology
University of Calcutta
University of Delhi
University of Kerala
University of Mumbai
Bennett University
Amity University
English Language requirements
To apply to any of our courses, you need to prove a minimum level of English language proficiency.
Royal Holloway is pleased to offer English Language requirement exemption for students who have completed either of the following:
MOI (Medium of Instruction): See the above section on "Acceptance of MOI from select Indian Universities".
Class 12 English Language: 70% for UG (valid for 2 years) and PGT study, and 80% for Research Degrees (both valid for 5 years)
Students who do not meet the English language requirements may be able to take a pre-sessional English language programme.
Fees and scholarships
Fees vary between courses each year. Specific information about fees can be found in the course finder entry for your chosen course.
You could be eligible for one of our undergraduate or postgraduate scholarships, including our dedicated scholarships for international students.
One of these scholarships is our Royal Holloway India Masters Scholarship 2026, which is a tuition fee reduction of £6,000 for Masters students currently living in India.
In addition to the above, there may also be other external funding available to you if you are considering postgraduate study at Royal Holloway,
The Local Indian Community
There is a very strong and vibrant Indian community at Royal Holloway. We have a Bhangra Society and a number of religious groups including Hindu, Islamic, Catholic, and Sikh.The Students' Union organise a weekly fruit and vegetable market on campus which includes a wide selection of Asian products.
London is recognised internationally as home to one of the largest Indian communities in the world, with 650,000 residents identifying as Indian in the city. West London in particular is home to large Indian communities, in Southall (known as 'Little India' or 'Little Punjab' and Hounslow (close to Heathrow Airport and home to a diverse professional community. The city is home to a large Indian professional community, with extensive opportunities for networking whilst studying here at Royal Holloway.

Alumni Insights
Sidhanth Puri (MSc Marketing, 2018)
I completed my MSc in Marketing at Royal Holloway, University of London from 2017–2018, and my experience there was truly life-changing. Living independently for the first time and being part of such a diverse international community helped me grow both personally and professionally. The exposure I gained through interacting with people from different cultures, along with RHUL’s teaching approach and well-structured curriculum, played a major role in shaping my confidence and global outlook.
What made my journey especially memorable was the supportive environment at RHUL. The professors were approachable and understanding towards international students, while the campus staff and security always made me feel safe, comfortable, and at home.
After graduating, I worked with American Express before joining and now leading my family’s hospitality consulting business, Sidh Inc. The confidence, adaptability, and international exposure I gained at RHUL continue to influence my entrepreneurial journey today.
Limabenla Jamir (M.Sc Applied Social Psychology)
My journey into global engagement, and development began at Royal Holloway, University of London, where I pursued an MSc in Applied Social Psychology. While Royal Holloway’s academic reputation initially drew me in, what truly stood out was its close-knit and intellectually vibrant community. The University pushed me beyond academics and encouraged me to develop a more critical and global perspective.
One of the most formative parts of my time at Royal Holloway was working alongside Dr. Hanna Zagefka, which led to my first international academic publication - Conflict, Fear and identity. That experience gave me an early introduction to research collaboration and the importance of using evidence-based approaches to understand social issues across cultures and communities.
Beyond the classroom, I became actively involved in the Royal Holloway Diplomatic Society, which introduced me to the international Model United Nations circuit. Participating and leading delegations to conferences such as Oxford MUN and London International MUN was transformative. It not only deepened my interest in social issues and international affairs, but also gave me the opportunity to engage with students from different departments, cultures, and countries across the university and beyond.
Those experiences inspired me to later establish the Northeast India International Model United Nations (NEIMUN), which, in its own small way, aimed to create opportunities for young people from my region to engage with global dialogue and leadership platforms. Royal Holloway also introduced me to some of my closest friends, people I remain connected with to this day and who continue to be among the most valued relationships in my life.
Over the last decade, my work has evolved into public policy and international development, with a focus on governance, youth engagement, and inclusive development. Looking back, Royal Holloway was more than a university experience for me it was the place that opened up an entirely different world and shaped the direction of my professional journey.
Transferring from University of London Teaching Centres
Students in India have the opportunity to study the Royal Holloway BSc Business Administration awarded by the University of London with academic direction by Royal Holloway with our University of London Regional Teaching Centres (RTCs) in India. The programme is available at the following RTCs:
Podar World College - Juhu (Mumbai)
Indian School of Business and Finance (New Delhi)
Russell Square International College (Mumbai)
MET Institute of International Studies (Mumbai)
Burhani College (Mumbai)
IILM Lodhi Road (New Delhi)
Students studying the BSc Business Administration can transfer to the following campus based courses at Royal Holloway:
BSc Business and Management (N200)
BSc Management with international business (N2N1)
BSc Management with Marketing (N2N5)
BSc Management with Human Resources (N2N6)
Applications should be submitted via UCAS by 1 August each year and are subject to the following requirements:
Year 2 entry - Conditional on achieving at least 50% overall in first year of distance learning course.
Year 3 entry - Conditional on achieving an average of at least 50% over two years of the distance learning course.
The above criteria are also subject to satisfactory references, personal statement and final approval from the Programme Director and Head of School.
Transferring students are exempt from English Language requirements.
Students applying for a transfer may be eligible for a Royal Holloway University of London Teaching Centre Scholarship. To be considered an applicant must be a BBA students studying at one of the UoL Teaching Centres who have an average of 65% or above, applying to progress into Year 2 or 3 of a Royal Holloway Business & Management Bachelor’s degree taught on RH campus. Applications must be made through the standard Royal Holloway scholarship application process:
Eligible students will submit a 400-word statement as part of the application
The University will shortlist and select successful candidates based on the rating criteria
The University then notifies both successful and unsuccessful candidates of their outcome
The deadline for applying for this scholarship is 9 April.
If you have any queries regarding the transfer process, please speak with your University of London coordinator at your current institution.
